# Local English demonstration audio

150 mono 16-bit PCM WAV files: 48 teaching symbols, 26 letter names and one
alphabet recording for each of two synthetic voices.

Generated by `interactive-lab/generate-audio.py`, using eSpeak NG via
`espeakng-loader==0.2.4`. The base `en` voice is English (Great Britain);
`en+f3` and `en+m3` use separate female and male voice configurations.
The runtime does not load eSpeak or send text/audio to an online service.

These are formant-synthesized demonstrations, not recordings of human
speakers. Explicit phoneme mnemonics prevent IPA characters being read as
letter names. Individual phonemes and blended articulation remain subject
to pedagogical review; waveform duration synchronization is not anatomical
forced alignment. Alphabet letter intervals are stored in `manifest.json`.

Isolated full vowels use explicit citation stress (schwa stays unstressed).
Long monophthongs use synthesis rate 95 and short ones 170 for a clearer
teaching contrast. Separate vowel mnemonics retain their distinct synthesis
targets; no PCM repetition or pitch shifting creates the long/short pairs.
This timing contrast is pedagogical, not a fixed natural-speech ratio.
Letter names retain rate 115. The manifest records the input, rate and
active duration for auditing; these checks do not certify perceived quality.

eSpeak NG project and source: https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng
eSpeak NG is GPL-3.0-or-later; the synthesis engine is a build dependency and
is not shipped in this web app. The generated audio contains only this
project's phoneme/letter inputs. Model attribution is separate in
`../ATTRIBUTION.md`.
